title: Z-residual Diagnostics for brms Logistic Regression
text: vignette demonstrates three distinct ways can use Zresidual evaluate Bayesian models fit via brms: Passing Custom User-Defined Function. Triggering Simulation-Predictive Function. Utilizing Built-Analytic Predictive Function. illustrate methods effectively, establish consistent testing environment. assume environment already contains pre-loaded list 100 datasets (sim_data), true log-odds follow non-linear sine wave. fit two models dataset: misspecified linear model correctly specified non-linear model. MCMC sampling computationally expensive, execute cache 200 model fits disk. subsequent sections, instantly load identical models demonstrate three Zresidual calling methods yield identical, reliable diagnostics.
code: if (!dir.exists(model_dir)) {   dir.create(model_dir, recursive = TRUE) }  n_sim <- 20 n_sample <- 200  sim_data <- vector("list", n_sim)  # Loop through iterations, checking for existing files before simulating/fitting for(i in 1:n_sim) {      data_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_", i, ".rds")   wrong_model_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i, ".rds")   correct_model_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i, ".rds")      # --- 1. Check and Handle Data ---   if (!force_refit && file.exists(data_file)) {     sim_data[[i]] <- readRDS(data_file)   } else {     # First-time running: Simulate the Bernoulli data     x <- runif(n_sample, 0, 10)     eta <- 2.5 * sin(x)     y <- rbinom(n_sample, 1, plogis(eta))          dat_i <- data.frame(y = y, x = x)     sim_data[[i]] <- dat_i     saveRDS(dat_i, file = data_file)   }      # --- 2. Check and Fit Wrong Model ---   if (force_refit || !file.exists(wrong_model_file)) {     brm(       y ~ x,        family = bernoulli(),        data = sim_data[[i]],       backend = "cmdstanr",       normalize = FALSE,       file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i),        refresh = 0,       cores = 4     )   }      # --- 3. Check and Fit Correct Model ---   if (force_refit || !file.exists(correct_model_file)) {     brm(       y ~ sin(x),        family = bernoulli(),        data = sim_data[[i]],       backend = "cmdstanr",       normalize = FALSE,       file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i),        refresh = 0,       cores = 4     )   } }

what: Zresidual Using a Custom User-Defined log_pointpred Function
title: Z-residual Diagnostics for brms Logistic Regression
text: Zresidual built highly extensible architecture. specific model family backend natively supported yet, simply want explicit control math, can bypass internal defaults entirely passing custom function log_pointpred argument. , define custom analytical function leverages brms::posterior_epred() manually extract expected probabilities (p) push R’s native distribution functions. evaluate model, explicitly map custom function log_pointpred argument. Zresidual handles rest randomization, prediction extraction, covariate binding automatically.       Replicated p-values fitted models Diagnostic Test p-values Across Randomized Replicates batching custom Zresidual call across 100 simulated datasets, construct sampling distribution. uniform p-values correctly specified model confirm providing user-defined function seamlessly integrates Zresidual statistical pipeline.
code: log_pointpred_brms_bern <- function(fit, data = NULL, ...) {      # 1. Resolve data   data_in <- if (is.null(data)) fit$data else data      # 2. Extract observed response safely   model.data <- model.frame(fit$formula, data = data_in)   model.var  <- names(model.data)      response <- fit$formula$resp   if (is.null(response) || !response %in% model.var) {     response <- all.vars(fit$formula$formula)[1]   }      y_obs <- as.numeric(model.data[[response]])   n <- length(y_obs)      # 3. Extract Posterior Expected Values (probabilities)   p <- brms::posterior_epred(fit, dpar = "mu", newdata = data_in, ...)   mc_used <- nrow(p)      # 4. Calculate Log-PMF and Log-Survival Functions   lpmf <- matrix(NA_real_, mc_used, n)   lsf  <- matrix(NA_real_, mc_used, n)      for (i in seq_len(n)) {     lpmf[, i] <- dbinom(y_obs[i], size = 1, prob = p[, i], log = TRUE)     lsf[, i]  <- pbinom(y_obs[i], size = 1, prob = p[, i],                            lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)   }      list(     log_like = lpmf,     log_surv  = lsf,     is_discrete = rep(1L, n)   ) } set.seed(123) ## for reproducibility # Load the first cached dataset and model pair dat <- readRDS(paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_1.rds"))  fit_wrong <- brm(y ~ x, family = bernoulli(), data = dat, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_1")) fit_correct <- brm(y ~ sin(x), family = bernoulli(), data = dat, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_1"))  # Call Zresidual explicitly using the custom function z_wrong   <- Zresidual(fit_wrong, data = dat, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 10, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_bern) z_correct <- Zresidual(fit_correct, data = dat, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 10, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_bern) i <- 1   qqnorm(z_wrong, irep = i, main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid Q-Q") plot(z_wrong, x_axis_var = "x", category = dat$y, irep = i,      main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid vs X") boxplot(z_wrong, x_axis_var = "lp", irep = i,         main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid vs LP") qqnorm(z_correct, irep = i, main.title = "Correct: Z-Resid Q-Q") plot(z_correct, x_axis_var = "x", category = dat$y, irep = i,      main.title = "Correct: Z-Resid vs X") boxplot(z_correct, x_axis_var = "lp", irep = i,         main.title = "Correct: Z-Resid vs LP") res_table <- data.frame(   "Replicate" = paste("Rep", 1:ncol(z_wrong)),   "SW_W"      = as.numeric(sw.test.zresid(z_wrong)),   "AOV_W"     = as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_wrong, X = "lp")),   "BL_W"      = as.numeric(bartlett.test.zresid(z_wrong, X = "lp")),   "SW_C"      = as.numeric(sw.test.zresid(z_correct)),   "AOV_C"     = as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_correct, X = "lp")),   "BL_C"      = as.numeric(bartlett.test.zresid(z_correct, X = "lp")) )  res_table %>%   kable(     digits = 4,      col.names = c("Replicate", "SW", "AOV", "Bartlett", "SW", "AOV", "Bartlett"),     caption = "Diagnostic Test p-values Across Randomized Replicates",     align = "lcccccc"   ) %>%   kable_styling(     bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE, position = "center"   ) %>%   add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Wrong Model (Linear)" = 3, "Correct Model (Non-linear)" = 3)) user_res_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/user_pvalues.rds")  if (!force_recalcz && file.exists(user_res_file)) {   res <- readRDS(user_res_file)   p_c <- res$p_c   p_w <- res$p_w } else {   p_c <- numeric(n_sim)   p_w <- numeric(n_sim)      for(i in 1:n_sim) {     dat_sim <- readRDS(paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_", i, ".rds"))     fit_w_sim <- brm(y ~ x, family = bernoulli(), data = dat_sim, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i), refresh = 0)     z_w_sim <- Zresidual(fit_w_sim, data = dat_sim, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_bern)     p_w[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_w_sim, X = "lp"))          fit_c_sim <- brm(y ~ sin(x), family = bernoulli(), data = dat_sim, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i), refresh = 0)     z_c_sim <- Zresidual(fit_c_sim, data = dat_sim, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_bern)     p_c[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_c_sim, X = "lp"))   }   saveRDS(list(p_c = p_c, p_w = p_w), user_res_file) } p_correct <- ggplot(   data.frame(p_value = p_c),   aes(x = p_value) ) +   geom_histogram(     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),     fill = "lightblue",     colour = "white"   ) +   geom_hline(     yintercept = n_sim / 10,     colour = "red",     linetype = 2   ) +   labs(     title = "Correct: Model P-values",     x = "p-value",     y = "Count"   ) +   theme_bw(base_size = 14) +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(       size = 15,       face = "bold",       hjust = 0.5     )   )  p_wrong <- ggplot(   data.frame(p_value = p_w),   aes(x = p_value) ) +   geom_histogram(     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),     fill = "salmon",     colour = "white"   ) +   labs(     title = "Wrong: Small P-values",     x = "p-value",     y = "Count"   ) +   theme_bw(base_size = 14) +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(       size = 15,       face = "bold",       hjust = 0.5     )   )  p_correct p_wrong

text: exact analytic mathematical formula either unknown computationally prohibitive specific model family, Zresidual provides robust simulation mechanism: Simulation-Predictive method. passing pred_method = "simulation", Zresidual automatically invokes model’s native simulate posterior_predict functions draw empirical bounds, bypassing need explicit PDF/CDF math entirely. Notice drop log_pointpred argument explicitly request "simulation" method. Zresidual automatically handles translation empirical draws normalized residuals.       Replicated p-values fitted models Diagnostic Test p-values Across Randomized Replicates Batching approach confirms simulation fallback statistically valid. generates identical expected behaviors (uniform distributions correct models, skewed distributions structural misspecifications) without requiring single line custom analytical code.

code: sim_res_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/sim_pvalues.rds")  if (!force_recalcz && file.exists(sim_res_file)) {   res <- readRDS(sim_res_file)   p_c <- res$p_c   p_w <- res$p_w } else {   p_c <- numeric(n_sim)   p_w <- numeric(n_sim)    for(i in 1:n_sim) {     dat_sim <- readRDS(paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_", i, ".rds"))          fit_w_sim <- brm(y ~ x, family = bernoulli(), data = dat_sim, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i))     z_w_sim <- Zresidual(fit_w_sim, data = dat_sim, pred_method = "simulation", mcmc_summarize = "iscv", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1)     p_w[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_w_sim, X = "lp"))          fit_c_sim <- brm(y ~ sin(x), family = bernoulli(), data = dat_sim, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i))     z_c_sim <- Zresidual(fit_c_sim, data = dat_sim, pred_method = "simulation", mcmc_summarize = "iscv", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1)     p_c[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_c_sim, X = "lp"))   }   saveRDS(list(p_c = p_c, p_w = p_w), sim_res_file) } plot_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 14) +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(       size = 15,       face = "bold",       hjust = 0.5     )   )  p_correct <- ggplot(   data.frame(p_value = p_c),   aes(x = p_value) ) +   geom_histogram(     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),     fill = "lightblue",     colour = "white"   ) +   geom_hline(     yintercept = n_sim / 10,     colour = "red",     linetype = 2   ) +   labs(     title = "Correct: Model P-values",     x = "p-value",     y = "Count"   ) +   plot_theme  p_wrong <- ggplot(   data.frame(p_value = p_w),   aes(x = p_value) ) +   geom_histogram(     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),     fill = "salmon",     colour = "white"   ) +   labs(     title = "Wrong: Misspecification P-values",     x = "p-value",     y = "Count"   ) +   plot_theme  p_correct p_wrong

routing z_wrong   <- Zresidual(fit_wrong, data = dat, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 10) z_correct <- Zresidual(fit_correct, data = dat, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 10) i <- 1   qqnorm(z_wrong, irep = i, main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid Q-Q") plot(z_wrong, x_axis_var = "x", category = dat$y, irep = i,      main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid vs X") boxplot(z_wrong, title: Demo of Component-wise Z-residual Diagnosis for Bayesian Hurdle Models
text: vignette demonstrates use Zresidual package compute component-wise Z-residuals diagnosing Bayesian hurdle models (Mullahy 1986). Based output brms package R (Bürkner 2017), Z-residuals can calculated separately zero, count, overall hurdle components reveal potential model misspecifications. systematically illustrate , simulate 100 datasets Hurdle Negative Binomial model fit two models : correctly specified HNB model misspecified HP model. evaluate single dataset comprehensively using visualizations, leverage 100 datasets examine sampling distribution diagnostic p-values.

what: Definitions of Component-wise Z-residuals for Bayesian Hurdle Models
title: Demo of Component-wise Z-residual Diagnosis for Bayesian Hurdle Models
text: logistic component modeling probability structural zeros. count component modeling positive counts using zero-truncated distribution. Let C_i \\{0, 1\}, C_i = 1 indicates non-zero value, C_i = 0 indicates zero value ^\text{th} observations. C_i=1, corresponding count model operates y_i^+ \\{1, 2, \dots\}, .e., positive counts . \pi^o_i : zero probability, \mu_i^{(t)}, \phi^{(t)} : parameters count component. given observation y_i^\text{obs}, component-wise posterior predictive PMF survival functions defined . p_i^{\text{post}, \pi^o_irdle}(y_i^\text{obs}) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \begin{cases} {\pi^o_i}^{(t)} & \text{} y_i^\text{obs} = 0, \\ (1 - {\pi^o_i}^{(t)}) \cdot\frac{p_i^\text{UT}(y_i^\text{obs} | \theta^{(t)})}{1 - p_i^\text{UT}(0 | \theta^{(t)})} & \text{} y_i^\text{obs} =1, 2, \ldots,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} S_i^{\text{post}, \pi^o_irdle}(y_i^\text{obs}) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \begin{cases} 1 & \text{} y_i^\text{obs} < 0, \\ 1-{\pi^o_i}^{(t)} & \text{} 0 \le y_i^\text{obs} < 1, \\ (1 - {\pi^o_i}^{(t)}) \cdot \frac{S_i^\text{UT}(y_i^\text{obs} \mid \theta^{(t)})}{1-p_i^\text{UT}(0 \mid \theta^{(t)})} & \text{} y_i^\text{obs} \ge 1. \end{cases} p_i^{\text{post}, \text{logit}}(c_i^\text{obs}) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \begin{cases} {\pi^o_i}^{(t)} & \text{} c_i^\text{obs} = 0, \\ 1 - {\pi^o_i}^{(t)} & \text{} c_i^\text{obs} = 1,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \tag{1} S_i^{\text{post}, \text{logit}}(c_i^\text{obs}) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \begin{cases} 1 & \text{} c_i^\text{obs} < 0, \\ 1-{\pi^o_i}^{(t)} & \text{} 0 \le c_i^\text{obs} < 1, \\ 0, & \text{} c_i^\text{obs} \ge 1. \end{cases} \tag{2} p_i^{\text{post},\text{count}}({y_i^+}^\text{obs}) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \begin{cases}     \frac{p_i^\text{UT}({y_i^+}^\text{obs} \mid \theta^{(t)})}{1 - p_i^\text{UT}(0 \mid \theta^{(t)})}, & \text{ } {y_i^{+}}^\text{obs} = 1,2,\ldots,\\     0 & \text{ otherwise.} \end{cases} \tag{3} S_i^{\text{post}, \text{count}}({y_i^+}^\text{obs}) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \begin{cases}     1 & \text{ } {y_i^+}^\text{obs} < 1 \\     \frac{S_i^\text{UT}({y_i^+}^\text{obs} \mid \theta^{(t)})}{1-p_i^\text{UT}(0 \mid \theta^{(t)})}, & \text{ } {y_i^+}^\text{obs} \ge 1 \end{cases} \tag{4} p_i^\text{UT}(. \mid \theta^{(t)}) S_i^\text{UT}(. \mid \theta^{(t)}) denote PMF survival function untruncated count distribution. observed value y_i^\text{obs}, define:  \text{rsp}_i(y_i^\text{obs} | \theta^{(t)}) = S_i(y_i^\text{obs} | \theta^{(t)}) + U_i \times p_i(y_i^\text{obs} | \theta^{(t)}) \tag{5} U_i \sim \text{Uniform}(0,1). , Z-residual discrete response variable :  z_i = -\Phi^{-1}(\text{rsp}_i(y_i^\text{obs}|\theta)) \sim N(0, 1) \tag{6}

what: Preparation: Data Simulation and Model Caching
title: Demo of Component-wise Z-residual Diagnosis for Bayesian Hurdle Models
text: simulate 100 datasets Hurdle Negative Binomial (HNB) process. dataset, fit two models: 1. Correct Model: Hurdle Negative Binomial (family = hurdle_negbinomial()). 2. Misspecified Model: Hurdle Poisson (HP), approximated forcing tight prior shape parameter (prior("normal(1000, 1)")), causes negative binomial heavily resemble Poisson distribution, restricting overdispersion. MCMC sampling computationally expensive, execute cache 200 model fits disk.
code: n_sim <- 20  n_sample <- 100  sim_data <- vector("list", n_sim)   for(i in 1:n_sim) {     data_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_", i, ".rds")    wrong_model_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i, ".rds")    correct_model_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i, ".rds")     #   # --- 1. Check and Handle Data ---    if (!force_refit && file.exists(data_file)) {      sim_data[[i]] <- readRDS(data_file)    } else {      x <- rnorm(n_sample)      z <- rnorm(n_sample)       # Hurdle (zero) part      logit_p <- -1 - 1 * x      p_zero <- exp(logit_p) / (1 + exp(logit_p))      zeros <- rbinom(n_sample, 1, p_zero)       # Count (non-zero) part      # FIX: Lowered intercept and slope to prevent exp() overflow      log_mu <- 1.5 + 2 * x      mu <- exp(log_mu)      size <- 6       # Generate from zero-truncated negative binomial      prob <- size / (size + mu)      y <- (1 - zeros) * distributions3::rztnbinom(n_sample, size, prob)       dat_i <- data.frame(y = y, x = x, z = z)      sim_data[[i]] <- dat_i      saveRDS(dat_i, file = data_file)    }     # --- 2. Check and Fit Misspecified Model (HP Approx) ---    if (force_refit || !file.exists(wrong_model_file)) {      tryCatch({        brms::brm(          bf(y ~ x + z, hu ~ x + z),          family = hurdle_negbinomial(),          prior = prior("normal(1000, 1)", class = "shape"),          data = sim_data[[i]],          backend = brms_backend,          file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i),          refresh = 0,          cores = 4,          # Optional: tighten control parameters for the tricky prior          control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)        )      }, error = function(e) {        message(sprintf("Iteration %d: Wrong model failed to fit - %s", i, e$message))      })    }     # --- 3. Check and Fit Correct Model (HNB) ---    if (force_refit || !file.exists(correct_model_file)) {      tryCatch({        brms::brm(          bf(y ~ x + z, hu ~ x + z),          family = hurdle_negbinomial(),          data = sim_data[[i]],          backend = brms_backend,          file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i),          refresh = 0,          cores = 4        )      }, error = function(e) {        message(sprintf("Iteration %d: Correct model failed to fit - %s", i, e$message))      })    }  }

title: Demo of Component-wise Z-residual Diagnosis for Bayesian Hurdle Models
text: Let’s load first dataset demonstrate Zresidual directly. compute Z-residuals models separately across logistic (zero), count, overall hurdle components using "post" summary method. Notice type mcmc_summarize passed directly arguments Zresidual(). following animations show component-wise QQ plots 10 randomized replicates correctly specified model. code: # Function to extract mean p-values across replicates get_pvals <- function(zres, zcov) {   c(     SW = mean(as.numeric(sw.test.zresid(zres))),     AOV = mean(as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(zres, X = "lp", zcov = zcov))),     BL = mean(as.numeric(bartlett.test.zresid(zres, X = "lp", zcov = zcov)))   ) }  res_c_zero <- get_pvals(zres_c_zero, zcov_c_zero) res_c_count <- get_pvals(zres_c_count, zcov_c_count) res_c_hurdle <- get_pvals(zres_c_hurdle, zcov_c_hurdle)  res_w_zero <- get_pvals(zres_w_zero, zcov_w_zero) res_w_count <- get_pvals(zres_w_count, zcov_w_count) res_w_hurdle <- get_pvals(zres_w_hurdle, zcov_w_hurdle)  table_df <- data.frame(   Component = c("Logistic (Zero)", "Count (+)", "Overall Hurdle"),   HNB_SW = c(res_c_zero["SW"], res_c_count["SW"], res_c_hurdle["SW"]),   HNB_AOV = c(res_c_zero["AOV"], res_c_count["AOV"], res_c_hurdle["AOV"]),   HNB_BL = c(res_c_zero["BL"], res_c_count["BL"], res_c_hurdle["BL"]),   HP_SW = c(res_w_zero["SW"], res_w_count["SW"], res_w_hurdle["SW"]),   HP_AOV = c(res_w_zero["AOV"], res_w_count["AOV"], res_w_hurdle["AOV"]),   HP_BL = c(res_w_zero["BL"], res_w_count["BL"], res_w_hurdle["BL"]) )  table_df %>%   gt() %>%   tab_spanner(label = "Correct (HNB) p-values", columns = starts_with("HNB_")) %>%   tab_spanner(label = "Misspecified (HP) p-values", columns = starts_with("HP_")) %>%   cols_label(     HNB_SW = "Shapiro-Wilk", HNB_AOV = "ANOVA", HNB_BL = "Bartlett",     HP_SW = "Shapiro-Wilk", HP_AOV = "ANOVA", HP_BL = "Bartlett"   ) %>%   fmt_number(columns = -Component, decimals = 4) %>%   cols_align(align = "center", columns = everything()) %>%   tab_style(     style = cell_text(weight = "bold", color = "red"),     locations = cells_body(columns = starts_with("HP_"), rows = Component != "Logistic (Zero)")   ) %>%   tab_options(table.width = pct(100), table.font.size = px(14))

title: Demo of Component-wise Z-residual Diagnosis for Bayesian Hurdle Models
text: prove behavior isn’t artifact single chosen dataset, analyze sampling distribution ANOVA p-values across 100 simulated datasets. Since misspecification lies solely variance non-zero outcomes, isolate Zresidual(..., type="count") diagnostics analysis.   resulting histograms validate methodology: correctly specified model generates uniformly distributed p-values across datasets, component-wise test misspecified model correctly consistently flags overdispersion defect low p-values.
code: ana_res_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/ana_pvalues.rds")  if (!force_recalcz && file.exists(ana_res_file)) {   res <- readRDS(ana_res_file)   p_c <- res$p_c   p_w <- res$p_w } else {   p_c <- numeric(n_sim)   p_w <- numeric(n_sim)      for(i in 1:n_sim) {     dat_sim <- readRDS(paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_", i, ".rds"))          # Extract Misspecified Model (HP)     fit_w_sim <- brm(bf(y ~ x + z, hu ~ x + z), family = hurdle_negbinomial(), prior = prior("normal(1000, 1)", class = "shape"), data = dat_sim, backend = brms_backend, file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i), refresh = 0)     z_w_sim <- Zresidual(fit_w_sim, data = dat_sim, type = "count", mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1)     zcov_w_sim <- Zcov(fit_w_sim, data = dat_sim, type = "count")     p_w[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_w_sim, X = "lp", zcov = zcov_w_sim))          # Extract Correct Model (HNB)     fit_c_sim <- brm(bf(y ~ x + z, hu ~ x + z), family = hurdle_negbinomial(), data = dat_sim, backend = brms_backend, file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i), refresh = 0)     z_c_sim <- Zresidual(fit_c_sim, data = dat_sim, type = "count", mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1)     zcov_c_sim <- Zcov(fit_c_sim, data = dat_sim, type = "count")     p_c[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_c_sim, X = "lp", zcov = zcov_c_sim))   }      saveRDS(list(p_c = p_c, p_w = p_w), ana_res_file) } p_correct <- ggplot(data.frame(p_value = p_c), aes(x = p_value)) +   geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),                  fill = "lightblue", colour = "white") +   geom_hline(yintercept = n_sim / 10, colour = "red", linetype = 2) +   labs(title = "Correct (HNB): Count Component P-values",        x = "p-value", y = "Count") +   theme_bw()  p_wrong <- ggplot(data.frame(p_value = p_w), aes(x = p_value)) +   geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),                  fill = "salmon", colour = "white") +   labs(title = "Misspecified (HP): Count Component P-values",        x = "p-value", y = "Count") +   theme_bw()  p_correct p_wrong

what: Preparation: Data Simulation and Model Caching
title: Z-residual Diagnostics for brms Poisson Regression
text: vignette demonstrates three distinct ways can use Zresidual evaluate Bayesian models fit via brms: Passing Custom User-Defined Function. Triggering Simulation-Predictive Function. Utilizing Built-Analytic Predictive Function. illustrate methods effectively, first generate consistent testing environment. simulate 100 datasets (true log-rate follows non-linear sine wave) fit two models : misspecified linear model correctly specified non-linear model. MCMC sampling computationally expensive, execute cache 200 model fits disk. subsequent sections, instantly load identical models demonstrate three Zresidual calling methods yield identical, reliable diagnostics.
code: if (!dir.exists(model_dir)) {   dir.create(model_dir, recursive = TRUE) }  n_sim <- 20 n_sample <- 200  sim_data <- vector("list", n_sim)  # Loop through iterations, checking for existing files before simulating/fitting for(i in 1:n_sim) {      data_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_", i, ".rds")   wrong_model_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i, ".rds")   correct_model_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i, ".rds")      # --- 1. Check and Handle Data ---   if (!force_refit && file.exists(data_file)) {     sim_data[[i]] <- readRDS(data_file)   } else {     x <- runif(n_sample, 0, 10)     y <- rpois(n_sample, exp(1.5 * sin(x)))          dat_i <- data.frame(y = y, x = x)     sim_data[[i]] <- dat_i     saveRDS(dat_i, file = data_file)   }      # --- 2. Check and Fit Wrong Model ---   if (force_refit || !file.exists(wrong_model_file)) {     brm(       y ~ x,        family = poisson(),        data = sim_data[[i]],       backend = "cmdstanr",       normalize = FALSE,       file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i),        refresh = 0,       cores = 4     )   }      # --- 3. Check and Fit Correct Model ---   if (force_refit || !file.exists(correct_model_file)) {     brm(       y ~ sin(x),        family = poisson(),        data = sim_data[[i]],       backend = "cmdstanr",       normalize = FALSE,       file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i),        refresh = 0,       cores = 4     )   } }

what: Zresidual Using a Custom User-Defined log_pointpred Function
title: Z-residual Diagnostics for brms Poisson Regression
text: Zresidual built highly extensible architecture. specific model family backend natively supported yet, simply want explicit control math, can bypass internal defaults entirely passing custom function log_pointpred argument. , define custom analytical function leverages brms::posterior_epred() manually extract expected rates (\lambda) push R’s native distribution functions. evaluate model, explicitly map custom function log_pointpred argument. Zresidual handles rest randomization, prediction extraction, covariate binding automatically.       Replicated p-values fitted models Diagnostic Test p-values Across Randomized Replicates batching custom Zresidual call across 100 simulated datasets, construct sampling distribution. uniform p-values correctly specified model confirm providing user-defined function seamlessly integrates Zresidual statistical pipeline.
code: log_pointpred_brms_pois <- function(fit, data = NULL, ...) {      # 1. Resolve data   data_in <- if (is.null(data)) fit$data else data      # 2. Extract observed response safely   model.data <- model.frame(fit$formula, data = data_in)   model.var  <- names(model.data)      response <- fit$formula$resp   if (is.null(response) || !response %in% model.var) {     response <- all.vars(fit$formula$formula)[1]   }      y_obs <- as.numeric(model.data[[response]])   n <- length(y_obs)      # 3. Extract Posterior Expected Values (lambda)   lambda <- brms::posterior_epred(fit, dpar = "mu", newdata = data_in, ...)   mc_used <- nrow(lambda)      # 4. Calculate Log-PMF and Log-Survival Functions   lpmf <- matrix(NA_real_, mc_used, n)   lsf  <- matrix(NA_real_, mc_used, n)      for (i in seq_len(n)) {     lpmf[, i] <- dpois(y_obs[i], lambda = lambda[, i], log = TRUE)     lsf[, i]  <- ppois(y_obs[i], lambda = lambda[, i],                            lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)   }      list(     log_like = lpmf,     log_surv  = lsf,     is_discrete = rep(1L, n)   ) } set.seed(123) ## for reproducibility # Load the first cached dataset and model pair dat <- readRDS(paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_1.rds"))  fit_wrong <- brm(y ~ x, family = poisson(), data = dat, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_1")) fit_correct <- brm(y ~ sin(x), family = poisson(), data = dat, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_1"))  # Call Zresidual explicitly using the custom function z_wrong   <- Zresidual(fit_wrong, data = dat, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 10, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_pois) z_correct <- Zresidual(fit_correct, data = dat, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 10, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_pois) i <- 1   qqnorm(z_wrong, irep = i, main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid Q-Q") plot( z_wrong,x_axis_var = "x", category = dat$y,irep = i,       main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid vs X", legend.position = "bottom", legend.nrow = 2) boxplot(z_wrong, x_axis_var = "lp", irep = i,         main.title = "Wrong: Z-Resid vs LP") qqnorm(z_correct, irep = i, main.title = "Correct: Z-Resid Q-Q") plot(z_correct,x_axis_var = "x", category = dat$y,irep = i,       main.title = "Correct: Z-Resid vs X",legend.position = "bottom") boxplot(z_correct, x_axis_var = "lp", irep = i,         main.title = "Correct: Z-Resid vs LP") res_table <- data.frame(   "Replicate" = paste("Rep", 1:ncol(z_wrong)),   "SW_W"      = as.numeric(sw.test.zresid(z_wrong)),   "AOV_W"     = as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_wrong, X = "lp")),   "BL_W"      = as.numeric(bartlett.test.zresid(z_wrong, X = "lp")),   "SW_C"      = as.numeric(sw.test.zresid(z_correct)),   "AOV_C"     = as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_correct, X = "lp")),   "BL_C"      = as.numeric(bartlett.test.zresid(z_correct, X = "lp")) )  res_table %>%   kable(     digits = 4,      col.names = c("Replicate", "SW", "AOV", "Bartlett", "SW", "AOV", "Bartlett"),     caption = "Diagnostic Test p-values Across Randomized Replicates",     align = "lcccccc"   ) %>%   kable_styling(     bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE, position = "center"   ) %>%   add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Wrong Model (Linear)" = 3, "Correct Model (Non-linear)" = 3)) user_res_file <- paste0(model_dir, "/user_pvalues.rds")  if (!force_recalcz && file.exists(user_res_file)) {   res <- readRDS(user_res_file)   p_c <- res$p_c   p_w <- res$p_w } else {   p_c <- numeric(n_sim)   p_w <- numeric(n_sim)      for(i in 1:n_sim) {     dat_sim <- readRDS(paste0(model_dir, "/data_sim_", i, ".rds"))     fit_w_sim <- brm(y ~ x, family = poisson(), data = dat_sim, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/wrong_sim_", i), refresh = 0)     z_w_sim <- Zresidual(fit_w_sim, data = dat_sim, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_pois)     p_w[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_w_sim, X = "lp"))          fit_c_sim <- brm(y ~ sin(x), family = poisson(), data = dat_sim, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0(model_dir, "/correct_sim_", i), refresh = 0)     z_c_sim <- Zresidual(fit_c_sim, data = dat_sim, mcmc_summarize = "post", randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1, log_pointpred = log_pointpred_brms_pois)     p_c[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_c_sim, X = "lp"))   }   saveRDS(list(p_c = p_c, p_w = p_w), user_res_file) } plot_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 14) +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(       size = 15,       face = "bold",       hjust = 0.5     )   )  p_correct <- ggplot(   data.frame(p_value = p_c),   aes(x = p_value) ) +   geom_histogram(     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),     fill = "lightblue",     colour = "white"   ) +   geom_hline(     yintercept = n_sim / 10,     colour = "red",     linetype = 2   ) +   labs(     title = "Correct: Model P-values",     x = "p-value",     y = "Count"   ) +   plot_theme  p_wrong <- ggplot(   data.frame(p_value = p_w),   aes(x = p_value) ) +   geom_histogram(     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),     fill = "salmon",     colour = "white"   ) +   labs(     title = "Wrong: Small P-values",     x = "p-value",     y = "Count"   ) +   plot_theme  p_correct p_wrong

code: if (!requireNamespace("Zresidual", quietly = TRUE)) {   if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")   remotes::install_github("tiw150/Zresidual", upgrade = "never", dependencies = TRUE) } library(Zresidual) library(survival) # Lightweight cumulative martingale comparator used in the original analysis script. lwy_cum_martingale <- function(fit, x, B = 1000, seed = 1) {   r <- residuals(fit, type = "martingale")   ok <- is.finite(r) & is.finite(x)   r  <- r[ok]   x  <- x[ok]    ord   <- order(x)   x_ord <- x[ord]   r_ord <- r[ord]   n     <- length(r_ord)    cum_obs <- cumsum(r_ord) / sqrt(n)   stat_obs <- max(abs(cum_obs))    set.seed(seed)   boot_mat  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = B, ncol = n)   boot_stat <- numeric(B)    for (b in seq_len(B)) {     w <- stats::rnorm(n)     cum_b <- cumsum(r_ord * w) / sqrt(n)     boot_mat[b, ] <- cum_b     boot_stat[b]  <- max(abs(cum_b))   }    list(     x = x_ord,     cum = cum_obs,     low = apply(boot_mat, 2, stats::quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),     high = apply(boot_mat, 2, stats::quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),     p = mean(boot_stat >= stat_obs)   ) }  # Capture a plotting method's return value while suppressing its automatic # print. This is needed only when several ggplot objects are combined. capture_zplot <- function(expr) {   tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")   grDevices::pdf(tmp)    on.exit({     grDevices::dev.off()     unlink(tmp)   }, add = TRUE)    force(expr) }

title: Z-residual Diagnostics for glm Logistic Regression
text: run simulation loop verify built-implementation correctly handles binomial data produces appropriate p-values.  Discussion: Correct Model, distribution p-values uniform, indicating well-specified model. Wrong Model, p-values small (clustered near 0), indicating ANOVA test successfully detected non-linear trend.
code: n_sim <- 100 sim_file <- paste0(file_prefix, "simulation_results.rds")  if (!force_rerun && file.exists(sim_file)) {   sim_res <- readRDS(sim_file)   p_c <- sim_res$p_c   p_w <- sim_res$p_w } else {   p_c <- numeric(n_sim)   p_w <- numeric(n_sim)   n_sample <- 200     for(i in 1:n_sim) {     x_sim <- runif(n_sample, 0, 10)          # Generate true non-linear data     eta_sim <- 2.5 * sin(x_sim)     y_sim   <- rbinom(n_sample, 1, plogis(eta_sim))     dat_sim <- data.frame(y = y_sim, x = x_sim)          # --- Case 1: Wrong Model (Linear) ---     fit_w <- glm(y ~ x, family = binomial(), data = dat_sim)     z_w   <- Zresidual(fit_w, data = dat_sim, randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1)     p_w[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_w, X = "x"))          # --- Case 2: Correct Model (Sine) ---     fit_c <- glm(y ~ sin(x), family = binomial(), data = dat_sim)     z_c   <- Zresidual(fit_c, data = dat_sim, randomized = TRUE, nrep = 1)     p_c[i] <- as.numeric(aov.test.zresid(z_c, X = "x"))   }      saveRDS(list(p_c = p_c, p_w = p_w), sim_file) } par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) hist(p_c, main = "Correct: Uniform p-values", xlab = "p-value", col = "lightblue", breaks = 20) abline(h = n_sim / 20, col = "red", lty = 2)  hist(p_w, main = "Wrong: Small p-values", xlab = "p-value", col = "salmon", breaks = 20)

what: Z-residual Using a Custom User-Defined log_pointpred Function
title: Z-residual Diagnostics for glm Poisson Regression
text: Since Zresidual highly extensible, can easily handle standard frequentist models like glm. frequentist model can viewed “Bayesian” model posterior consisting exactly 1 draw (point estimate). , define custom analytic function log_pointpred_glm_poisson extracts predicted rates (\lambda) using standard predict() function structures 1 \times N matrix format expected Zresidual. retrieve first cached dataset evaluate glm fits using custom function.       Replicated p-values fitted models Diagnostic test p-values across randomized replicates utilize identical cached datasets verify custom glm implementation correctly detects misspecifications across 100 simulations.  Discussion: uniform distribution p-values correctly specified glm model confirms Zresidual perfectly handles standard frequentist output provided 1 \times N matrix via custom predictive function. Conversely, strongly skewed distribution linear specification demonstrates test reliably catches structural misspecifications, mirroring results saw Bayesian brms framework.
code: log_pointpred_glm_poisson <- function(fit, data = NULL, ...) {      # 1. Resolve data   data_in <- if (is.null(data)) model.frame(fit) else data      # 2. Extract observed response   # For glm objects, the response variable name can be extracted from the formula   resp_var <- all.vars(formula(fit))[1]   y_obs <- as.numeric(data_in[[resp_var]])   n <- length(y_obs)      # 3. Extract Point Estimate Expected Values (lambda)   # type = "response" gives the predicted rate (lambda) on the outcome scale   lambda <- predict(fit, newdata = data_in, type = "response")      # 4. Calculate Log-PMF and Log-Survival Functions   # We format these as 1 x N matrices because there is only 1 "draw"   lpmf <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 1, ncol = n)   lsf  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 1, ncol = n)      for (i in seq_len(n)) {     lpmf[1, i] <- dpois(y_obs[i], lambda = lambda[i], log = TRUE)     lsf[1, i]  <- ppois(y_obs[i], lambda = lambda[i], lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)   }      list(     log_like = lpmf,     log_surv  = lsf,     is_discrete = rep(1L, n)   ) } # code: log_pointpred_glm_poisson <- function(fit, data = NULL, ...) {      # 1. Resolve data   data_in <- if (is.null(data)) model.frame(fit) else data      # 2. Extract observed response   # For glm objects, the response variable name can be extracted from the formula   resp_var <- all.vars(formula(fit))[1]   y_obs <- as.numeric(data_in[[resp_var]])   n <- length(y_obs)      # 3. Extract Point Estimate Expected Values (lambda)   # type = "response" gives the predicted rate (lambda) on the outcome scale   lambda <- predict(fit, newdata = data_in, type = "response")      # 4. Calculate Log-PMF and Log-Survival Functions   # We format these as 1 x N matrices because there is only 1 "draw"   lpmf <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 1, ncol = n)   lsf  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 1, ncol = n)      for (i in seq_len(n)) {     lpmf[1, i] <- dpois(y_obs[i], lambda = lambda[i], log = TRUE)     lsf[1, i]  <- ppois(y_obs[i], lambda = lambda[i], lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)   }      list(     log_like = lpmf,     log_surv  = lsf,     is_discrete = rep(1L, n)   ) }

title: Z-Residual Diagnostic Tool for Assessing Covariate Functional Form
text: use Z-residuals diagnose shared-frailty models Cox proportional hazards setting unspecified baseline hazard. Suppose g groups individuals, group containing n_i individuals, = 1,\ldots,g. Let y_{ij} possibly right-censored observation jth individual group , let \delta_{ij} indicate whether observation uncensored. randomized survival probability (RSP) y_{ij} S_{ij}^{R}(y_{ij}, \delta_{ij}, U_{ij}) = \begin{cases} S_{ij}(y_{ij}),   & \text{} \delta_{ij}=1,\\ U_{ij}S_{ij}(y_{ij}),   & \text{} \delta_{ij}=0, \end{cases} U_{ij} uniform random variable (0,1) S_{ij}(\cdot) postulated survival function given covariates x_{ij}. y_{ij} censored, S_{ij}^{R} randomized 0 S_{ij}(y_{ij}). true model, RSPs uniformly distributed (0,1) given x_i. can therefore transformed residuals desired reference distribution. use standard normal quantile: r_{ij}^{Z}(y_{ij}, \delta_{ij}, U_{ij}) = -\Phi^{-1}\left\{ S_{ij}^{R}(y_{ij}, \delta_{ij}, U_{ij}) \right\}. true model, residuals follow standard normal distribution. Consequently, diagnostic methods developed normal regression can also used censored data. normal transformation also makes extremely small large RSPs easier identify; even small number extreme values may indicate model misspecification.

title: Z-Residual Diagnostic Tool for Assessing Covariate Functional Form
text: example illustrates Z-residuals diagnose overall GOF functional form covariates analysis survival times patients acute myeloid leukemia. dataset contains 411 patients recorded M. D. Anderson Cancer Center 1980 1996. patients age 60 came 24 administrative districts. available prognostic factors include age, sex, white blood cell count (wbc) diagnosis, Townsend score (tpi), higher values indicate less affluent areas. censoring rate 29.2%. response survival time days study entry death censoring. Preliminary analysis showed wbc highly right-skewed. logarithmic transformation often used reduce influence extremely large covariate values, may also mask relationship outcome.
code: leuksurv_path <- system.file(   "extdata",   "LeukSurv.rda",   package = "Zresidual" )  if (nzchar(leuksurv_path)) {   load(leuksurv_path) } else {   # Compatibility with package versions that exposed the dataset through data().   data("LeukSurv", package = "Zresidual", envir = environment()) }  if (!exists("LeukSurv")) {   stop("The LeukSurv dataset could not be loaded.", call. = FALSE) }  LeukSurv$district <- as.factor(LeukSurv$district) LeukSurv$sex <- as.factor(LeukSurv$sex) LeukSurv$logwbc <- log(LeukSurv$wbc + 0.001) LeukSurv <- droplevels(LeukSurv[LeukSurv$age < 60, ]) if (requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)) {   DT::datatable(     LeukSurv,     caption = "Table 1: Acute myeloid leukemia survival data.",     options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)   ) } else {   knitr::kable(     head(LeukSurv, 20),     caption = "Table 1: Acute myeloid leukemia survival data (first 20 rows)."   ) }

title: Z-residual: A Unified Gaussian-like Residual for Checking Bayesian and Frequentist Models with Continuous, Discrete, and Censored Response
text: Zresidual package implements diagnostic residuals based predictive distribution observation. utilizing full probabilistic information model, package generates residuals approximately normally distributed, enabling standard graphical numerical diagnostics identical used Gaussian OLS. foundation approach Randomized Survival Probability (RSP). given observation y_i, RSP represents value predictive survival function y_i, incorporating randomization term ensure continuity discrete outcomes. defined Equation 1: \text{RSP}_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) + U_i \, p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) \tag{1} : S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = P(Y_i > y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) survival function (probability new observation strictly exceed observed value). p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = P(Y_i = y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) probability mass function (PMF). continuous outcomes, p_i(y_i) = 0, term drops entirely. U_i \sim \text{Uniform}(0,1) random uniform variable. role continuously “smear” discrete probability mass, ensuring resulting RSP suffer discrete steps. correctly specified model, RSP follows uniform U(0,1) distribution. Z-residual derived transforming RSP via inverse standard normal cumulative distribution function (\Phi^{-1}), shown Equation 2: z_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = -\Phi^{-1}[\text{RSP}_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})] \tag{2} correct model specification, residuals follow standard normal N(0,1) distribution. mapping allows researchers assess quality predictive distribution—including mean, variance, shape—using familiar, highly sensitive Gaussian diagnostics. survival analysis, framework naturally extends carefully defining predictive distribution observed outcome. Let T_i true underlying event time continuous survival function S_i^*(t | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = P(T_i > t | \boldsymbol{\theta}). Let C_i censoring time, assumed independent T_i. observed outcome Y_i = \min(T_i, C_i), record event indicator \delta_i = (T_i \le C_i). Thus, observed data point y_i, dual nature depending \delta_i: event observed (\delta_i = 1): Y_i behaves continuous variable. probability surviving strictly past y_i S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = S_i^*(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}). outcome continuous point, probability mass zero: p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = 0. event right-censored (\delta_i = 0): know T_i > C_i = y_i. perspective observed variable Y_i, point y_i acts accumulation probability mass representing possible future event times. Therefore, probability strictly surviving past censored point zero: S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = 0. probability mass point exactly probability true event happens censoring time: p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = S_i^*(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}). Formally, predictive survival probability mass functions observed outcome Y_i defined : S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = \begin{cases} S_i^*(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}), & \text{} \delta_i = 1 \\ 0, & \text{} \delta_i = 0 \end{cases} \tag{3} p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) = \begin{cases} 0, & \text{} \delta_i = 1 \\ S_i^*(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}), & \text{} \delta_i = 0 \end{cases} \tag{4} substituting context-specific definitions S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) back general RSP equation Equation 1, obtain unified, piecewise formula censored data Equation 5: \text{RSP}(y_i | \delta_i,\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \left\{ \begin{array}{rl} S_i^*(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}), & \text{} \delta_i=1 \\ U_i \, S_i^*(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}), & \text{} \delta_i=0 \end{array} \right. \tag{5} Just standard regression, RSPs transformed Z-residuals via normal quantile function, defined Equation 6: z_i(y_i, \delta_i, U_i) = -\Phi^{-1} (\text{RSP}(y_i| \delta_i, \boldsymbol{\theta})) \tag{6} Normal transformation highlights extreme RSPs indicate model misspecification (proportional hazards violations) often masked standard Martingale Cox-Snell residuals.

title: Z-residual: A Unified Gaussian-like Residual for Checking Bayesian and Frequentist Models with Continuous, Discrete, and Censored Response
text: practice, true parameter vector \boldsymbol{\theta} unknown must estimated data. package supports two primary paradigms constructing residuals accounting estimation uncertainty. frequentist models (e.g., stats::glm, survival::coxph, glmmTMB), parameters treated fixed unknowns. package computes residuals simply substituting maximum likelihood estimate (MLE), denoted \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}, directly predictive distributions: \text{RSP}_i(y_i | \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) = S_i(y_i | \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) + U_i \, p_i(y_i | \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \tag{7} plug-approach computationally instantaneous, uses data y twice (estimate \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} calculate residual y_i). specific models like coxph, package provides cross-validatory Z-residuals prevent artificial deflation residual variance occurs double-use, allowing rigorous validation. Bayesian paradigm, parameters \boldsymbol{\theta} described posterior distribution \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y). account parameter uncertainty, Zresidual integrates point-wise RSP posterior space. posterior RSP defined averaging predictive survival probability mass functions full-data posterior: \text{RSP}_i^{\text{post}}(y_i) = \int S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y) d\boldsymbol{\theta} + U_i \int p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y) d\boldsymbol{\theta} \tag{8} Given sample T draws, \{\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}\}_{t=1}^T, posterior via MCMC, integrals estimated using Monte Carlo averages survival mass functions: \widehat{S}_i^{\text{post}}(y_i) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) \quad \text{} \quad \widehat{p}_i^{\text{post}}(y_i) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) \tag{9} estimated posterior RSP simply randomized combination: \widehat{\text{RSP}}_i^{\text{post}}(y_i) = \widehat{S}_i^{\text{post}}(y_i) + U_i \, \widehat{p}_i^{\text{post}}(y_i) \tag{10} posterior Z-residual derived transforming averaged probability: z_i^{\text{post}}(y_i) = -\Phi^{-1}(\widehat{\text{RSP}}_i^{\text{post}}(y_i)) \tag{11} simple compute, approach involves double-use data. However, standardizing procedure “summarize first, test,” Z-residuals remain asymptotically N(0,1) hypothesis test p-values asymptotically Uniform(0,1). provide rigorous diagnostic avoids double-use, consider leave-one-cross-validation (LOOCV). cross-validatory RSP, \text{RSP}_i^{\text{cv}}(y_i), averaged posterior conditioned data except y_i, denoted y_{-}: \text{RSP}_i^{\text{cv}}(y_i) = \int S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y_{-}) d\boldsymbol{\theta} + U_i \int p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y_{-}) d\boldsymbol{\theta} \tag{12} Re-running MCMC analysis n times calculate directly computationally prohibitive. Instead, Zresidual efficiently approximates using full-data posterior sample via importance sampling. importance weights given ratio target LOO posterior full-data posterior, simplifies inverse likelihood left-observation: w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \frac{1}{f_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})} \propto \frac{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y_{-})}{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y)} \tag{13} Using weights, compute ISCV survival mass functions weighted Monte Carlo averages: \widehat{S}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = \frac{\sum_{t=1}^T S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})}{\sum_{t=1}^T w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})} \tag{14}  \widehat{p}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = \frac{\sum_{t=1}^T p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})}{\sum_{t=1}^T w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})} \tag{15} estimated ISCV RSP combines weighted components: \widehat{\text{RSP}}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = \widehat{S}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) + U_i \, \widehat{p}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) \tag{16} Finally, ISCV Z-residual defined : z_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = -\Phi^{-1}(\widehat{\text{RSP}}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i)) \tag{17} Similar deleted residuals OLS, ISCV Z-residuals typically exhibit variance slightly greater 1, offering heightened sensitivity influential outliers model misspecification.

However, standardizing procedure “summarize first, test,” Z-residuals remain asymptotically N(0,1) hypothesis test p-values asymptotically Uniform(0,1). provide rigorous diagnostic avoids double-use, consider leave-one-cross-validation (LOOCV). cross-validatory RSP, \text{RSP}_i^{\text{cv}}(y_i), averaged posterior conditioned data except y_i, denoted y_{-}: \text{RSP}_i^{\text{cv}}(y_i) = \int S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y_{-}) d\boldsymbol{\theta} + U_i \int p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}) \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y_{-}) d\boldsymbol{\theta} \tag{12} Re-running MCMC analysis n times calculate directly computationally prohibitive. Instead, Zresidual efficiently approximates using full-data posterior sample via importance sampling. importance weights given ratio target LOO posterior full-data posterior, simplifies inverse likelihood left-observation: w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \frac{1}{f_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})} \propto \frac{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y_{-})}{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta} | y)} \tag{13} Using weights, compute ISCV survival mass functions weighted Monte Carlo averages: \widehat{S}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = \frac{\sum_{t=1}^T S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})}{\sum_{t=1}^T w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})} \tag{14}  \widehat{p}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = \frac{\sum_{t=1}^T p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})}{\sum_{t=1}^T w_i^{\text{}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})} \tag{15} estimated ISCV RSP combines weighted components: \widehat{\text{RSP}}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = \widehat{S}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) + U_i \, \widehat{p}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) \tag{16} Finally, ISCV Z-residual defined : z_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i) = -\Phi^{-1}(\widehat{\text{RSP}}_i^{\text{iscv}}(y_i)) \tag{17} Similar deleted residuals OLS, ISCV Z-residuals typically exhibit variance slightly greater 1, offering heightened sensitivity influential outliers model misspecification.

Whether analyzing Bayesian shared frailty model frequentist GLM, core algorithm requires pointwise predictive likelihoods survival probabilities. extend Zresidual new model class family, developers users need provide function (conventionally named log_pointpred_<class>_<family>) accepts fitted model data, returns list containing exactly three elements: log_surv: M \times N numeric matrix log-survival probabilities (\log S_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})), M number posterior draws (M=1 frequentist models) N number observations. Note Note: right-censored observations (y_i \delta_i = 0), probability surviving strictly past censoring time zero (S_i(y_i) = 0). Consequently, corresponding entries log_surv matrix set -Inf. log_like: M \times N numeric matrix observation-wise log-likelihoods. Crucially, definition likelihood always model-wide specification; depends whether specific observation y_i acts discrete continuous point. m-th posterior draw, defined : \text{log\_like} (\boldsymbol{\theta}^{(m)},y_i) = \begin{cases} \log p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(m)}), & \text{} y_i \text{ discrete right-censored} \\ \log f_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(m)}), & \text{} y_i \text{ continuous uncensored} \end{cases} Understanding Shifting Role log_like exact mathematical function log_like matrix shifts depending observation type residual estimation method: 1. Posterior frequentist Z-residuals Training Test Data Discrete/Censored Data: log_like strictly required. supplies \log(p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})) term necessary calculate Randomized Survival Probability (RSP). Continuous Data: log_like effect. true probability mass continuous point zero, RSP calculation ignores matrix entirely relies solely survival function. 2. Bayesian ISCV Z-residuals Training Data Discrete/Censored Data: log_like strictly required plays dual role. used calculate RSP serves likelihood derive importance-sampling weights (w_i \propto 1/p_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})). Continuous Data: log_like strictly required. ignored RSP calculation , continuous PDF \log(f_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})) mathematically essential calculate importance weights (w_i \propto 1/f_i(y_i | \boldsymbol{\theta})) approximate leave-one-posterior. Table 1: Summary log_like Requirements is_discrete: integer vector length N 1 indicates y_i discrete/censored, 0 indicates continuous/uncensored. tells package exactly interpret corresponding column log_like matrix observation--observation basis. isolating model-specific predictive extraction single function, Zresidual can automatically handle randomization, integration, cross-validation, statistical testing hood.

title: An Animation for Understanding Z-residuals
text: Zresidual package implements diagnostic residuals based predictive distribution observation. utilizing full probabilistic information model, package generates residuals approximately normally distributed. allows standard diagnostic techniques similar using Pearson residuals OLS regression. given observation y_i, Randomized Survival Probability (RSP)—also known randomized probability integral transform—represents value predictive survival function (upper-tail probability) y_i, adjusted randomization term ensure continuity discrete outcomes. defined : RSP_i(y_i \mid \theta) = S_i(y_i \mid \theta) + U_i \, p_i(y_i \mid \theta) \tag{1} S_i p_i represent survival function probability mass function, respectively, derived predictive distribution y_i given covariates \mathbf{x}_i parameters \theta. U_i \sim \text{Unif}(0,1) random uniform variable used smooth discrete outcomes. correctly specified model—observed data y_i arises assumed predictive distribution—RSP follows \text{Unif}(0,1) distribution. Z-residual (aka randomized quantile residual) derived transforming RSP via inverse survival function N(0,1): z_i(y_i \mid \theta) = -\Phi^{-1}\left(RSP_i(y_i \mid \theta)\right)= \Psi^{-1}\left(RSP_i(y_i \mid \theta)\right) \tag{2} \Psi^{-1}(p) = -\Phi^{-1}(p) = \Phi^{-1}(1-p) represents inverse survival function (upper-tailed quantile) standard normal distribution N(0,1). words, Z-residual simply N(0,1) value shares upper-tail area (RSP) observed y_i. transformation effectively maps predictive distribution standard normal scale preserving tail probabilities. model correct, resulting Z-residuals follow standard normal distribution. Intuition: Think Z-residual distance median, rescaled account skewness smoothed handle discreteness. ensures residual +2 always implies degree ‘extremeness’, regardless original distribution’s shape.

text: Zresidual package implements diagnostic residuals based predictive distribution observation. utilizing full probabilistic information model, package generates residuals approximately normally distributed, enabling standard diagnostics Pearson’s residuals OLS. foundation approach Randomized Survival Probability (RSP). given observation y_i, RSP represents value predictive cumulative distribution function (CDF) y_i, randomization term ensure continuity discrete outcomes. defined : \text{RSP}_i(y_i \mid \theta) = S_i(y_i \mid \theta) + U_i \, p_i(y_i \mid \theta) S_i p_i represent survival function probability mass function, respectively, derived predictive distribution y_i given covariates \mathbf{x}_i parameters \theta. U_i \sim \text{Unif}(0,1) random uniform variable used handle discrete outcomes. correctly specified model observed data y_i arises assumed predictive distribution, RSP follows \text{Unif}(0,1) distribution. Z-residual derived transforming RSP via inverse standard normal cumulative distribution function: z_i^{\text{RSP}}(y_i \mid \theta) = -\Phi^{-1}[\text{RSP}_i(y_i \mid \theta)] correct model specification, residuals follow standard normal N(0,1) distribution. mapping allows researchers assess quality predictive distribution—including mean, variance, shape—using standard diagnostics Gaussian OLS. practical applications, parameter vector \theta must estimated. package supports several paradigms constructing residuals evaluating model fit: Plugging Point Estimates: Calculating residuals fixing \theta specific value, MLE posterior mean. Posterior Averaging: Integrating residuals posterior distribution \theta given training data. Importance Sampling: Reweighting MCMC draws posterior distribution estimate residuals. title: Compute residual diagnostics for supported survival models — surv_residuals
code: if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   n <- 30   x <- rnorm(n)   t_event <- rexp(n, rate = exp(0.3 * x))   t_cens  <- rexp(n, rate = 0.5)   status  <- as.integer(t_event <= t_cens)   time    <- pmin(t_event, t_cens)   dat <- data.frame(time = time, status = status, x = x)    fit <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ x, data = dat)   r <- surv_residuals(fit, data = dat, residual.type = "martingale")   head(as.vector(r)) } #> [1]  0.9017249 -0.9004452  0.7137561  0.4771257  0.3631152  0.8328093
